claim_text: JPMorganChase reported Q2 2026 net income of $16.9 billion, EPS of $6.14, and ROTCE of 23%, excluding significant items.

claim_text: Firm revenue was up 15% year-on-year, driven by Markets revenue, higher AWM/CCB asset management fees, higher IB revenue, and higher deposit and loan balances, partially offset by lower rates.
quote: revenue was up 15% year-on-year, predominantly driven by Markets revenue, higher asset management fees in AWM and CCB, higher Investment Banking revenue, and higher deposit and loan balances, partially offset by the impact of lower rates.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Expenses of $27.3 billion were up 15% year-on-year, largely driven by volume/revenue-related expense and front-office hiring/labor inflation.
quote: Expenses of $27.3 billion were up 15% year-on-year, largely driven by volume and revenue-related expense, as well as growth in front office hiring and labor inflation.

claim_text: Credit costs were $2.5 billion, with net charge-offs of $2.4 billion and a net reserve build of $149 million.

quote: This quarter's standardized RWA increase of approximately $103 billion is largely driven by increases in financing across our Markets business, as well as growth in traditional lending.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: The Board intends to increase the quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share, effective in the third quarter.
quote: the Board intends to increase the quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share effective in the third quarter.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

quote: CCB reported net income of $5.3 billion. Revenue of $20.3 billion was up 8% year-on-year, predominantly driven by higher Card NII, largely on higher revolving balances, as well as higher operating lease income in Auto and asset management fees in Wealth Management.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: In Banking & Wealth Management, average deposits were up 3% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter, driven by net new checking account growth of over 500,000 accounts this quarter.
quote: average deposits were up 3% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter, driven by strong net new checking account growth of over 500,000 accounts this quarter.

claim_text: CIB reported net income of $9.7 billion; revenue of $24.9 billion was up 27% year-on-year, with IB fees up 30% year-on-year on double-digit growth across all products.
quote: the CIB reported net income of $9.7 billion. Revenue of $24.9 billion was up 27% year-on-year, driven by strong performance across the businesses. IB fees were up 30% year-on-year, reflecting double-digit growth across all products, with particularly strong performance in equity underwriting.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: IB performance this quarter was helped by large ECM deals and accelerated M&A closures, but management sees the underlying pipeline as robust and expects activity to remain healthy.
quote: While this quarter's performance was supported by both some large ECM deals and the acceleration of the closure of some M&A transactions, the pipeline remains quite robust and the current activity levels seem to be encouraging more activity. As a result, while conversion will obviously be dependent on market conditions, we expect activity levels to remain healthy.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: In Markets, Fixed Income revenue was up 6% year-on-year and Equities revenue was up 86% year-on-year, an exceptionally strong quarter driven by highly dynamic market conditions.
quote: In Markets, Fixed Income was up 6% year-on-year, with solid performance in Credit, Currencies and Emerging Markets, and Rates, partially offset by lower revenue in Commodities. The equities business delivered an exceptionally strong quarter, with revenue up 86% year-on-year, reflecting the highly dynamic market conditions.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Management views this quarter's Equities strength as difficult to repeat statistically, even though it could recur.
quote: I just think like statistically, it seems improbable that that particular combination of effects could repeat itself. But it obviously could.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: AWM reported net income of $2 billion with a 38% pre-tax margin; revenue of $6.9 billion was up 19% year-on-year; AUM of $5.1 trillion was up 18% year-on-year and client assets of $7.7 trillion were up 19% year-on-year.
quote: AWM reported net income of $2 billion, with pre-tax margin of 38%. Revenue of $6.9 billion was up 19% year-on-year, driven by growth in management fees on higher average market levels and strong net inflows, as well as investment valuation gains, higher loan balances and higher brokerage activity.

claim_text: AWM long-term net inflows were $50 billion this quarter, with continued strength across Fixed Income and Equity; AUM of $5.1 trillion was up 18% year-on-year.
quote: Long-term net inflows were $50 billion, with continued strength across Fixed Income and Equity. AUM of $5.1 trillion was up 18% year-on-year and client assets of $7.7 trillion were up 19% year-on-year, driven by higher market levels and continued net inflows.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Management raised FY2026 NII ex. Markets guidance to about $96.5 billion, total NII to about $105.5 billion (Markets NII rising to about $9 billion), adjusted expense outlook to about $107.5 billion, and now expects the Card net charge-off rate to be approximately 3.2%.
quote: we now expect NII ex. Markets to be about $96.5 billion and total NII to be approximately $105.5 billion as a function of Markets NII increasing to about $9 billion. And the new adjusted expense outlook is about $107.5 billion, with the increase Jeremy Barnum Chief Financial Officer, JPMorganChase primarily due to higher volume- and revenue-related expenses, driven by the activity levels and associated revenue outperformance. Finally, we now expect Card net charge-off rate to be approximately 3.2%, reflecting better-than-expected consumer credit performance.

claim_text: Management explicitly raised full-year NII ex. Markets guidance from $95 billion to $96.5 billion.
quote: revising up from $95 billion to $96.5 billion for the full year
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

quote: we did revise up this year's expense guidance by $2.5 billion, which is not a trivial number
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Barnum explains the expense guidance increase: the capital markets complex outperformed the company's own prior expectations by $6.5 billion in H1, and $1.5 billion of additional expense has already been booked against that outperformance.
quote: in the first half of this year, the capital markets complex has outperformed our then expectations by $6.5 billion, and we have booked in the first half of the year $1.5 billion of additional expenses associated with that.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Barnum explains that Markets NII guidance rose despite higher rates because of a shift in balance sheet composition (fewer financed non-interest-bearing assets expected in H2), which can overwhelm the usual rate effect.
quote: the difference is changes in balance sheet composition, essentially expecting lower amounts of financed non-interest bearing assets on the balance sheet in Jeremy Barnum Chief Financial Officer, JPMorganChase the second half of the year.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Management flags a negative-convexity risk in consumer deposit pricing: if rates rose enough to trigger a meaningfully different regime, the rate paid on consumer deposits could accelerate beyond what current EaR (earnings-at-risk) models assume.
quote: when we do our stress testing and when we think about not just like slightly more elevated inflation environment and a slightly more aggressive response from the Fed, but something that's like meaningfully different, that's a true stress test with an actual change in regime, one of the things that we look at and stress is like, okay, at what point do you have that kind of like acceleration in rate paid as a result of that type of environment.
speaker: Jeremy Barnum

claim_text: Management describes a mild but broad-based loosening in competitors' credit underwriting standards -- more aggressive revenue assumptions, more PIK, weaker covenants and more rollover risk in some segments -- while noting it is more pronounced among some lenders than others.
quote: I think we talked about it as a very mild one, but it's across several spectrum, which is people – assumptions on revenue growth or add-back of expenses, more PIK, some weaker – and this is not across the board, by the way. It's more some players than others. Some weaker covenants. Some people taking more rollover risk.
speaker: Jamie Dimon
